Policy on Video Recording of Classes for Fully Online or Mixed Mode Teaching 
 
 
 
Background 
 
1. Face-to-face classes were susp ended, towards the end of Semester 1 and two weeks after 
classes for Semester 2, 2019/20 had started, due to the social unrest and the outbreak of 
COVID-19 respectively. All classes, except lab/studio/practicu m-based sessions, have 
been delivered online since then.

Problems identified 
 
2. In the past two semesters, numerous students voiced out prob lems which had adversely 
affected their synchronous (real-time) online learning. These problems include: 
i) No Wi-Fi at home or in the remote residential regions; 
ii) Unstable Wi-Fi – slow internet, Wi-Fi connection failure / not working; 
iii) Insufficient mobile dat a for online classes; and 
iv) Different time zones, etc. 
 
3. These are genuine difficulties and problems

3. These are genuine difficulties and problems that are beyond students’ control. The 
University agrees that such problems must be properly addressed. 
 
 
 
Proposal 
 
Rationale 
 
1. To enhance students’ learning through synchronous online cla sses, it is proposed that all 
classes delivered in the fully online or mixed mode should be v ideo recorded and made 
available so that students can revisit the classes after the scheduled class hours. 
 
2. At present, recordings are available fo

urs. 
 
2. At present, recordings are available for some courses but no t for others. The policy will 
facilitate a consistent and uniform practice for all teachers a nd students. It will also help 
alleviate difficulties caused to and complaints from students d ue to the different 
arrangement among courses. 
 
International and Local Practices 
 
3. HKBU is not the first or only local institution which asks t eachers to record their classes 
and make them available to students. CityU, HKUST, P

d make them available to students. CityU, HKUST, PolyU and L U state it clearly to 
students that video recordings of classes will be uploaded for students' reference. In fact, 
CityU and HKUST have implemented video recording of face-to-face classes long before 
the 2019/20 academic year. 
 
4. Video recording of classes has also been practised at HKBU f or some face-to-face classes.

5. Many overseas institutions s uch as The London School of Econ omics and Political 
Science (LSE) in the UK and Nany ang Technological University (N TU) in Singapore 
have institutionalized video re cording of classes for over 10 y ears, when face-to-face 
classes were the norm. 
 
6. Experience sharing by LSE and NTU suggests that the majority of students do not skip 
classes due to the availability of lecture recordings. 
 
Recording, Share to Students and Retention 
 
7. To safeguard securi

o Students and Retention 
 
7. To safeguard security, all recordings will be done by the co urse instructors, and shared 
with their students in the respective courses via Google drive and Moodle together, which 
is only accessible through the BUniPort. 
 
8. A time-limit will be placed on the sharing. Course instructo rs may decide when to remove 
the recorded classes and should inform students of the arrangement in advance. In general, 
course instructors will remove the recordings from their

instructors will remove the recordings from their Google drive and the links in 
Moodle after the semester has come to an end. 
 
9. As soon as the sharing period is over, course instructors ca n save the recordings on their 
own computer for records and use. The University will not arch ive the recordings 
separately. 
 
10. For recordings saved at the ZOOM cloud, ZOOM cloud will hold them for 120 days. The 
University has not archived any recordings from the ZOOM cloud, and will not start this

dings from the ZOOM cloud, and will not start this 
practice. The University will remind colleagues to clear recordings from the ZOOM cloud 
at the end of every semester to make room for the new semester. 
 
Privacy and Copyright Issues 
 
11. The copyright of the recordings belongs to individual ins tructors and the University will 
not use the recordings without the individuals' consent. As far as the University is 
concerned, the ONLY purpose of the recordings is to facilitate students’ onlin

of the recordings is to facilitate students’ online access to 
classes. 
 
12. On the issue of whether videotaping of the classes and ma king them available to students 
would violate the principle “Use of Data” under the Personal Da ta (Privacy) Ordinance, 
if individual students have made comments or responses at classes, it should be noted that 
when enrolling as HKBU students, students would need to confirm the following: 
 
“The University may use my personal data for different academic and

ay use my personal data for different academic and administrative 
purposes which are in relation to my study at the University.” 
 
With the agreement of students and that the video recordings of classes and making them 
available to students are solely for academic purposes, there i s no violation to the “Use 
of Data” principle. 
 
13. To avoid that the recordings may be misused and sent to outside parties by students, stern 
reminders as follows will be put into Moodle and in general ann oun

ows will be put into Moodle and in general ann ouncements to staff and 
students:

 All video recordings of classes are for teaching and l earning purposes of the 
respective course. No part of the recordings of the classes sho uld be dubbed and/or 
made available to persons not enrolled in the course without th e explicit consent of the 
course instructor;

3. Rationale
In using digital technology for learning and teaching, we:
● adhere to a learner-centred approach;
● cater for students with a variety of abilities, aspirations and backgrounds; 
● integrate virtual and physical means to enhance teaching, learning, self-study, and collaboration
beyond limitations of distance and time; and
● strive for fit-for-purpose deployment of resources.
